MARITAL SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT

This Marital Settlement Agreement (this "Agreement") is made on September 9, 2026 between Adaeze Nwachukwu-Hollis, residing at 812 Kestrel Lane, Bloomington, Minnesota 55420 ("Wife"), and Tobias Nwachukwu-Hollis, residing at 41 Ridgeway Terrace, Apartment 3B, Saint Paul, Minnesota 55104 ("Husband"). Wife and Husband are each a "Party" and together the "Parties."

RECITALS

A. The Parties were married on June 21, 2014 in Hennepin County, Minnesota.

B. The Parties separated on March 2, 2026 and have lived apart since that date.

C. Two children were born of the marriage: Chidinma Nwachukwu-Hollis, born April 8, 2017, and Emeka Nwachukwu-Hollis, born January 30, 2020 (together, the "Children").

D. A dissolution proceeding is pending in the District Court, Fourth Judicial District, Hennepin County, Minnesota, Court File No. 27-FA-26-3891.

E. Each Party has had the opportunity to consult independent counsel, has made a full and fair disclosure of income, assets, and debts, and enters into this Agreement freely and without coercion.

F. The Parties wish to settle all questions of custody, parenting time, child support, spousal maintenance, and the division of property and debt.

1. LEGAL AND PHYSICAL CUSTODY

1.1 Legal Custody. The Parties shall have joint legal custody of the Children, and shall confer with one another on major decisions concerning the Children's education, non-emergency health care, and religious upbringing. If the Parties cannot agree after a good-faith conference, they shall attend one session with a parenting consultant before either seeks relief from the Court.

1.2 Physical Custody. The Parties shall have joint physical custody, with the Children's residence alternating under the parenting-time schedule in Section 2.

1.3 Best Interests. The Parties agree that this arrangement is in the best interests of the Children under Minnesota Statutes section 518.17, and acknowledge that the Court retains jurisdiction to determine custody and parenting time notwithstanding this Agreement.

2. PARENTING TIME

2.1 Regular Schedule. The Children shall be with Wife from Monday after school until Thursday morning drop-off, and with Husband from Thursday after school until Monday morning drop-off, on alternating weeks beginning September 14, 2026.

2.2 Holidays. Holiday parenting time is set forth in Schedule A and supersedes the regular schedule.

2.3 Summer. Each Party shall have two nonconsecutive weeks of uninterrupted vacation time each summer, on sixty (60) days' written notice, with Wife choosing first in even-numbered years and Husband first in odd-numbered years.

2.4 Transportation. The Party beginning parenting time provides transportation.

2.5 Relocation. Neither Party may move the Children's residence out of Minnesota without the other Party's written consent or a court order, as Minnesota Statutes section 518.175, subdivision 3 requires.

2.6 Communication. Each Party shall keep the other informed of the Children's school, medical, and activity schedules, and shall permit reasonable telephone and video contact with the other Party during that Party's parenting time.

3. CHILD SUPPORT

3.1 Guideline Calculation. Wife's gross monthly income is $7,400 and Husband's is $5,950. Applying the Minnesota child support guidelines under Minnesota Statutes section 518A.34 with the parenting-time expense adjustment, Husband shall pay Wife basic child support of $612 per month, beginning October 1, 2026, payable on the first day of each month.

3.2 Medical Support. Wife shall maintain health and dental insurance for the Children through her employer while it is available at reasonable cost. The Parties shall share unreimbursed medical, dental, orthodontic, and mental-health expenses for the Children 55% by Wife and 45% by Husband, in proportion to their incomes, and shall reimburse one another within thirty (30) days of a documented request.

3.3 Child Care. Work-related child care costs shall be shared in the same proportions.

3.4 Income Withholding. Child support shall be paid by income withholding as Minnesota Statutes section 518A.53 requires, through the Minnesota Child Support Payment Center.

3.5 Cost-of-Living Adjustment. Child support is subject to the biennial cost-of-living adjustment provided by Minnesota Statutes section 518A.75.

3.6 Duration. Child support for each child continues until that child attains the age of 18, or 20 if still attending secondary school, marries, becomes emancipated, or dies, whichever occurs first.

3.7 Dependency Exemptions. Wife shall claim Chidinma and Husband shall claim Emeka for federal and state income tax purposes each year, provided the claiming Party is current on child support as of December 31 of that year. Each Party shall sign IRS Form 8332 as needed.

4. SPOUSAL MAINTENANCE

4.1 Amount and Duration. Husband shall pay Wife spousal maintenance of $900 per month for forty-eight (48) months, beginning October 1, 2026 and ending September 1, 2030.

4.2 Termination. Maintenance terminates earlier on the death of either Party or on Wife's remarriage.

4.3 Modifiability. Maintenance is modifiable on a showing of a substantial change in circumstances under Minnesota Statutes section 518A.39. The Parties have considered and rejected a Karon waiver, and the Court retains jurisdiction over maintenance.

4.4 Taxes. Because this Agreement is executed after December 31, 2018, maintenance is not deductible by the payor and is not includable in the payee's income under section 11051 of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017.

5. REAL PROPERTY

5.1 Homestead. The Parties own the homestead at 812 Kestrel Lane, Bloomington, Minnesota, valued at $438,000, subject to a mortgage with a balance of $261,000. Wife shall have exclusive occupancy and shall receive the homestead as her sole property. Husband shall execute a quit claim deed to Wife within thirty (30) days after entry of the Judgment and Decree.

5.2 Refinance. Wife shall refinance the mortgage to remove Husband's name within twelve (12) months after entry of the Judgment and Decree. If Wife cannot refinance within that period, the homestead shall be listed for sale and the net proceeds divided as Section 5.3 provides.

5.3 Equalization. Wife shall pay Husband an equalization payment of $88,500, representing his share of the homestead equity, payable at refinance or sale, and secured by a lien against the homestead until paid.

6. PERSONAL PROPERTY, ACCOUNTS, AND RETIREMENT

6.1 Personal Property. The Parties have divided their household goods, furnishings, and personal effects to their mutual satisfaction, and each shall retain what is now in that Party's possession.

6.2 Vehicles. Wife shall receive the 2022 Subaru Outback and Husband the 2019 Toyota Tacoma, each subject to its own loan, and each Party shall indemnify and hold the other harmless from the loan on the vehicle that Party receives.

6.3 Bank Accounts. Each Party shall retain the accounts held in that Party's own name as of the date of separation.

6.4 Retirement. Husband's 401(k) with Larkspur Industries had a balance of $214,000 on the date of separation. Wife shall receive $53,500 of that balance by qualified domestic relations order, together with gains and losses from the date of separation to the date of transfer. The Parties shall share equally the cost of preparing the order, and the Court retains jurisdiction to enter and amend it until it is accepted by the plan administrator.

7. DEBTS

Each Party shall pay, and shall indemnify and hold the other harmless from, the debts listed opposite that Party's name on Schedule B. Neither Party has incurred any debt in the other's name since the date of separation, and neither shall do so hereafter.

8. RELEASES AND WAIVERS

Except for the obligations this Agreement creates, each Party releases the other from all claims arising out of the marriage, including any claim to the other's property, income, or estate, and each waives any right to take against the other's will, to a statutory elective share, to homestead rights, and to any interest as a surviving spouse.

9. GENERAL

9.1 Full Disclosure. Each Party has exchanged a complete statement of income, assets, and debts, and each relies on the other's disclosure. If either Party has failed to disclose an asset worth more than $2,500, the other may seek relief from the Court, and this Agreement is not a bar to that relief.

9.2 Independent Counsel. Wife is represented by Marchetti & Oyelaran, PLLC. Husband has been advised to obtain counsel, has had a reasonable opportunity to do so, and has chosen to proceed without counsel. Husband acknowledges that Wife's counsel does not represent him and has given him no legal advice.

9.3 Incorporation. This Agreement shall be incorporated into the Judgment and Decree of dissolution but shall not be merged into it, and shall survive as an independent contract enforceable by its own terms.

9.4 Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Minnesota.

9.5 Modification. Except for the provisions concerning the Children and spousal maintenance, which remain subject to the Court's continuing jurisdiction, this Agreement may be modified only by a writing signed by both Parties and approved by the Court.

9.6 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, with Schedules A and B, is the entire agreement between the Parties and supersedes all prior discussions and understandings.

9.7 Severability. If any provision is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force and effect.

9.8 Counterparts. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts and delivered electronically.

Each Party has read this Agreement, understands it, and signs it freely.

/s/ Adaeze Nwachukwu-Hollis
Adaeze Nwachukwu-Hollis, Wife
Dated: September 9, 2026

/s/ Tobias Nwachukwu-Hollis
Tobias Nwachukwu-Hollis, Husband
Dated: September 9, 2026
